consumers: thumb-regress (C++17, installed package only; three separate processes)

results.checks_per_platform: 159 named checks on Linux and macOS, 158 on Windows (the thread-count check is Linux/macOS only); every check passed; the three platforms' check-name sets are equal apart from that one
results.regression_consumer: thumb-regress runs lru-write -> lru-verify -> cache as three separate processes and reports the same 9 named checks on all three platforms; all pass. The checks were written against the public ABI that existed at the reviewed source, and were run there first (see history.red_4313315c): 6 of them failed, which is the reproduction being fixed.

review_findings.1_atomic_index_replace: Fixed with a platform atomic replace: MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING|WRITE_THROUGH) on Windows, rename(2) elsewhere. Reporting: rth_cache_open and rth_cache_clear now return RTH_IO when the index cannot be published and rth_stats.index_failures counts it; before the fix the same situation returned RTH_OK (red run, all three platforms: 'index that cannot be atomically replaced' :: status 0). Honest correction to the review premise: the assumed Windows failure of a rename onto an existing target did NOT reproduce on the windows-2022 runner (the MSVC STL maps std::filesystem::rename to a replacing MoveFileEx), so the 'touch -> close -> independent reopen -> smaller bound' identity check passed at the unfixed source on all three platforms. The identity assertion is kept as a permanent per-platform check ('regress: LRU recency written by one process survives an independent reopen', 'reopening with a smaller entry bound evicts the stale entry, not the touched ones', entries 2, 8x8 hit, 4x4 hit, 6x6 miss on Linux/Windows/macOS).
review_findings.2_temporary_safety: Reproduced on all three platforms: with 80 hard links planted (from a cancel callback) at the pre-0.1.0 temporary names, the unfixed store truncated the external sentinel (sentinel intact 0) and open deleted another process's fresh temporary. Fixed with exclusive create (O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW / CREATE_NEW|FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT) under an unpredictable per-open name plus a same-directory atomic replace, no-follow reads, and a 600 s grace before a current-naming temporary is treated as stale. Green: seeded 80, sentinel intact 1, links intact 1; live temporary preserved (4 bytes); stale temporary removed.
review_findings.3_bounded_scan: Reproduced: 1200 recognised candidates with max_entries=4 left 0 files, i.e. the whole directory was adopted and removed. Fixed with one bounded pass (budget 256 + max_entries*8, capped at 65536), entry-by-entry retention and eviction, and an explicit truncation flag. Green: 272 candidates inspected of 1300, 912 left untouched, retained entries 0, unrelated files kept, cache still stores and serves; a 40-entry reopen with max_entries=3 reports scanned_files 41 and peak_retained_entries 3 on every platform.
review_findings.4_reentry_and_exception_boundary: Reproduced: rth_cache_stats inside a control callback returned RTH_OK (status 0) while the header promises refusal, and on Windows an unrepresentable directory path terminated the process inside rth_cache_open (no check line, no summary in the red run). Fixed: every entry point that takes a cache uses the same owner/busy guard (stats, clear, find, cover/preview, close), a refused close leaves the cache alive, and every entry point catches std::bad_alloc (RTH_MEMORY) and other exceptions (RTH_IO). Green: stats/clear/find/cover all RTH_ARGUMENT inside the callback, outer call completes, cache usable; the unrepresentable path returns RTH_IO on Windows and macOS and RTH_OK with a byte-named directory on Linux, never terminating.

results.observed_sdk_behaviour: A PNG whose IHDR declares 30000x30000 over invalid data is refused by exr_image_page_dimensions as a damaged header (EXR_FORMAT), not EXR_LIMIT; the first run asserted LIMIT and failed on all three platforms. The check now accepts a refusal status LIMIT or FORMAT before decode and separate valid oversize PNGs assert LIMIT strictly. The SDK also refuses to import an EPUB that declares a cover item whose file is missing, so the cover-less case uses a generated EPUB with no cover item. Unchanged by this revision.

measurements_raw.note: Recorded numbers only; no performance is granted. RSS values are whole-process figures taken in the probe and process_peak_rss is cumulative across scenarios. cache_bytes is the on-disk .rth byte total of the scratch directory; for the overflow scenario it counts the candidates the bounded scan deliberately left untouched, while the retained cache is empty (entries 0). scanned_files and peak_retained_entries are the bounded-scan work and the largest retained entry set of that open, not RSS.
